questions.question: Explain Botha's reforms and the formation of the UDF and COSATU.
questions.expected_answer: Botha PM 1978: total onslaught, total strategy (reform plus security); black unions 1979; mixed-marriage laws repealed 1985. 1983 constitution (referendum November 1983): Tricameral Parliament (House of Assembly, Representatives, Delegates); white house dominant; executive State President (Botha 1984); Africans excluded (homelands, Black Local Authorities). Low turnout August 1984 (about 30% coloured, 20% Indian of registered). UDF launched 20 August 1983, Mitchells Plain, about 560 organisations; Boesak; Freedom Charter; leaders Albertina Sisulu, Gumede, Lekota. National Forum (BC). COSATU 1 December 1985, Durban, about half a million members, Barayi.

questions.question: Describe internal resistance and repression in the 1980s.
questions.expected_answer: Vaal uprising 3 September 1984 (rents, councillors, Sam Dlamini killed); army in Sebokeng October 1984; school boycotts, rent boycotts, consumer boycotts (Eastern Cape), street committees, civics; November 1984 stay-away; "ungovernable" call 1985. Violence: necklacing, people's courts, condemned by many leaders; UDF/ANC-Inkatha conflict, security force support for Inkatha. Repression: partial emergency 21 July 1985, national 12 June 1986 renewed to 1990; tens of thousands detained, children, torture; media restricted; UDF restricted 1988; Langa near Uitenhage 21 March 1985 (about 20 killed); Cradock Four June 1985; Vlakplaas, CCB; witdoeke vigilantes; raids on Maseru 1982, Gaborone 1985; End Conscription Campaign; Mass Democratic Movement defiance 1989.

questions.question: Explain the external pressures and moves towards negotiation by 1989.
questions.expected_answer: Rubicon speech 15 August 1985; Chase Manhattan refused loans; rand fell; debt standstill September 1985. US Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act October 1986 over Reagan's veto; EC, Commonwealth measures; Thatcher opposed broad sanctions; disinvestment (Barclays, GM, IBM); sports and cultural boycotts; Wembley concert June 1988. Cuito Cuanavale 1987-88, December 1988 agreements, Namibia independent March 1990; Berlin Wall November 1989. Secret talks: Mandela from 1985, met Botha 5 July 1989; Dakar 1987. Botha's stroke January 1989, resigned August 1989; De Klerk State President September 1989; Sisulu released October 1989.
